title: The Wuchang Uprising, 1911 — the accidental bomb that ended imperial China
sources: Wikipedia: 1911 Revolution — revolutionaries intent on overthrowing the Qing dynasty had built bombs, and on 9 October one of them accidentally exploded; the Qing Viceroy tried to track down and arrest the revolutionaries; they decided not to delay and launched the revolt; the revolution ended China's last imperial dynasty

Wikipedia: Wuchang Uprising — with their identities revealed, revolutionaries in the New Army faced imminent arrest; on the evening of 10 October they mutinied and captured the Viceroy's residence; the Viceroy fled; Sun Yat-sen was in the United States raising money, received a telegram he could not decipher and learned of the uprising from a newspaper the next morning; eighteen provinces seceded by the end of December; on 1 January 1912 the Republic of China was declared with Sun as first president; on 12 February 1912 the abdication of the Qing throne was announced on behalf of Puyi
Wikipedia: Puyi — became emperor at the age of two; the abdication edict was signed on his behalf in 1912
Wikipedia: Sun Yat-sen — the revolution 'ended over 2000 years of imperial rule in China'
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1846 William Lassell discovers Triton, Neptune's largest moon; 1903 Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women's Social and Political Union
Archive film (public domain, Wikimedia Commons): 'China: The Roots of Madness' (1967 US documentary; its early-20th-century shots are labelled illustrative); 'Wanrong and Puyi in 1924'

Photos (public domain): revolutionary soldiers prepare to attack Hankow, 1911; Hubei Military Government; imperial troops on the way to Hankow, 1911; Sun Yat-sen, 1911; Puyi with his father and brother, 1909; Puyi in the Forbidden City; the abdication edict, 12 February 1912

post.facebook:
On this day in 1911, the Wuchang Uprising began — and with it the revolution that ended China's last imperial dynasty.

Revolutionaries had been secretly building bombs to overthrow the Qing. On 9 October one of them exploded by accident; the authorities came looking, and the plotters' names were exposed. Facing arrest, the soldiers in the plot struck first on the evening of 10 October. The governor fled, and Wuchang was theirs.

The revolution's leader, Sun Yat-sen, was in the United States raising money. He couldn't decipher the telegram about it, and read the news in a newspaper the next morning. Within weeks, province after province broke away. On 1 January 1912 Sun became the first president of the Republic of China, and on 12 February the abdication was announced on behalf of the last emperor, Puyi — who was six years old.

Also on 10 October: Triton, Neptune's largest moon, was discovered (1846), and Emmeline Pankhurst founded the WSPU (1903).

youtube.description:
On 9 October 1911, a revolutionaries' bomb exploded by mistake in Wuchang, China. Exposed and facing arrest, the soldiers in the plot rose up the next day — 10 October — and took the city. Their leader, Sun Yat-sen, was in America and read about it in a newspaper. Within months the Republic of China was declared, and the last emperor, Puyi, gave up the throne at the age of six.

Also on 10 October: Triton is discovered (1846), Emmeline Pankhurst founds the WSPU (1903).
